column4: Pixel-art game character sprites in exactly the same style as the reference image, a mid-1990s Build-engine game like Duke Nukem 3D, Blood or Redneck Rampage: the same coarse pixel size, the same limited palette, the same shading and the same dark outline. A character turnaround model sheet: five full-body views of one and the same person standing upright and relaxed, arms hanging down, side by side in a single row, evenly spaced with clear magenta gaps between them, all exactly the same height and scale with the feet on one common baseline near the bottom edge: (1) seen straight from the front, (2) a three-quarter view from the front with the body turned toward the right edge of the image, (3) an exact side profile facing the right edge of the image, (4) a three-quarter view from behind, turned away toward the right edge of the image so the back and the right shoulder show, (5) seen straight from behind, the back of the head and the back of the clothes. Every figure is exactly the person in the reference image, with the same face, hair, body, proportions, clothes, colours and things they carry, nothing added and nothing left out: a young man in his twenties, a tired face, short messy dark brown hair and no hat or cap, a faded dark green zip-up windbreaker worn open with a small round orange camp patch on the left chest, a grey hoodie under it with the hood down, worn blue jeans with mud stains, muddy green rubber boots, a ring of keys on the belt, a black rubber flashlight held low in his right hand pointing at the ground. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around and between the figures, no ground, no floor line, no shadows, no text, no labels, no numbers, no grid lines, no frames, no borders, no watermark.
